SHOPLIFTER STOPPED BY CUSTOMER
MELAKA, Tues. – A man in his early 30s was caught stealing from a convenience store yesterday
afternoon. According to witnesses, the man was seen slipping several items into his backpack
before heading towards the exit without paying. A quick-thinking customer noticed the suspicious

detain him until the police arrived.

3.text:
PART 3
Questions 19 to 26 are based on the following passage
Read the passage carefully and choose the correct answer (A, B, C or D)
Electricity is one of the most important discoveries in human history. It powers almost every
aspect of modern life, from lighting and communication to transportation and industrial
production. Without electricity, we would not have the everyday comforts and technology we
depend on.
Electricity is a form of energy resulting from the movement of electrons. It can be generated in
various ways, including through the burning of fossil fuels such as coal, oil and natural gas.
However, because these fuels harm the environment, more people are turning to renewable
energy. These include solar power, wind energy, hydroelectric dams and geothermal energy.
These alternatives are not only better for the planet, but they also help reduce pollution and
combat climate change.
The journey of electricity begins at power plants, where it is generated and then travels long
distances through high-voltage cables. It eventually reaches homes, schools, hospitals and
businesses, enabling people to carry out tasks with speed and efficiency. In fact, most daily
activities depend on a constant supply of electricity. We use it to cook food, refrigerate food,
clean clothes, study and entertain ourselves. In industries, electricity powers machines and
technology, helping boost the economy and productivity.
Despite its many advantages, electricity must be used with caution. Improper handling of
electrical appliances or exposure to faulty wiring can result in serious accidents, such as electric
shocks or even fires. Using electrical appliances incorrectly or having bad wiring can cause
serious accidents like shocks or fires.
Another important issue is energy conservation. Although electricity is widely available in many
parts of the world, it is still a limited resource in others. Furthermore, the overuse of electricity
leads to higher energy consumption and increased pollution, especially if it comes from non-
renewable sources. To save electricity, we can adopt simple habits like switching off lights and
fans when they are not needed, unplugging devices after use and choosing energy-efficient
appliances.
Governments and organizations around the world are also encouraging the use of green
technologies. Innovations such as electric vehicles and solar panels are becoming more popular.
These not only reduce our dependence on fossil fuels but also promote a cleaner, healthier
environment.
In conclusion, electricity is an essential part of modern life. It has transformed the way we live,
work and interact with the world around us. As users, we must learn to appreciate its value, use
it responsibly and support eco-friendly ways to generate electricity. By doing so, we can ensure
that future generations will continue to benefit from the power of electricity without harming
the planet.
3.correction: Electricity is a natural phenomenon rather than a manufactured invention.

PART 4
Questions 27 to 32 are based on an article about a new way of travelling called glamping.
Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences (A to H) the one
which fits each gap (27–32). There are two extra sentences which you do not need to use.
Glamorous Adventures: The Rise of Glamping
For years, people associated camping with roughing it out—pitching tents, cooking over a
fire and sleeping on the cold hard ground. But times have changed and now a new trend has taken
over the world of outdoor adventures: glamping, a blend of "glamorous" and "camping". (27)
Glamping offers travellers the opportunity to enjoy the beauty of nature without giving up the
comforts of modern living.
The popularity of glamping has skyrocketed over the past decade, especially among young
globetrotters. Unlike traditional camping, glamping provides amenities such as plush beds, Wi-Fi,
private bathrooms and even air-conditioning. (28) This allows tourists to connect with
nature while still enjoying a hotel-like experience.
Glamping sites can be found all over the world, from the deserts of Morocco to the forests
of Japan. In Malaysia, eco-friendly resorts in Sabah and Pahang now offer glamping domes with
stunning views. (29) These unique accommodations appeal to environmentally conscious
travellers who still want luxury. Many travel experts believe glamping is not just a passing trend
but part of a larger shift towards sustainable tourism. (30) By minimising damage to
ecosystems and supporting local communities, glamping contributes to more responsible tourism.
Some critics, however, argue that glamping takes away the authenticity of real camping.
(31) They claim that the very essence of camping is to disconnect from technology and
embrace simplicity. Despite these criticisms, glamping continues to gain traction. The travel
industry has responded with creativity, designing tree houses, yurts and safari tents that blend style
and nature. (32) The result is a growing market that satisfies both adventure seekers and
comfort lovers.
So, whether you are sipping herbal tea under the stars or waking up to the sound of birds
in a soft king-sized bed, glamping offers an unforgettable travel experience. For many, it is the
perfect compromise between outdoor exploration and indoor relaxation.

A This hybrid approach is especially appealing to those who are not fond of the
traditional camping experience.
B After all, how can one feel adventurous when there are a minibar and a rain shower
nearby?
C Some resorts even offer personalised butler services and gourmet meals cooked by
professional chefs.
D These domes use low-impact designs to reduce disturbance to their surroundings.
E Critics argue that even eco-friendly camps can strain local water supplies and
generate excess.
F These luxurious outdoor experiences now cater to honeymooners, families and
solo travellers alike.
G It reflects the growing desire among tourists to explore the world in a more
meaningful and sustainable way.
H Many glamping locations host cultural evenings, such as storytelling around the
campfire.
4.correction: Sentence D now fits the eco-friendly domes paragraph rather than overlapping with sentence A.

PART 5
Questions 33 to 40 are based on the following texts.
Read the texts carefully and answer the questions that follow.
LET’S TALK ABOUT SMART SPENDING!
A. -Amir
I used to spend my pocket money on things like trendy gadgets and branded shoes. But after
attending a school workshop, I realised there’s a difference between needs and wants. Needs are
things we can’t live without, like food, clothes, and shelter. Wants are nice to have, but not
necessary—like limited-edition sneakers. Now, I would think twice before spending.
B. -Sophia
One day, I walked into a store just to look around—but walked out with a new smartwatch I
hadn’t planned to buy. It was on sale, and I thought it was a “limited-time offer.” Later, I
regretted it. I realised I was impulse buying—making a quick decision without thinking it
through. Now I always make a list before shopping and stick to it. It can reduce unnecessary
spending and improve financial discipline too.
C. -Siti
I bought a hair dryer online, but when it arrived, it didn’t work. At first, I wasn’t sure what to do.
Then I remembered what my teacher said about consumer rights. Everyone has the right to get
safe products, clear information, and fair service. I contacted the seller and asked for a
replacement—and got it!
D. -Jay
I love using e-wallets when I want to buy food or books. It’s fast and easy. But my older brother
reminded me to be careful with digital payments. If you’re not cautious, your personal details
could be stolen. While these methods offer convenience and speed, users must alert and protect
their personal information to avoid fraud or theft. Now, I will make sure to log out of my
accounts and never share my PIN with anyone.
E – Chong
I wanted to buy a new backpack. Instead of buying the first one I saw, I checked a few websites
to compare prices. In the end, I found the same bag at a lower price with free shipping. I believe
price comparison really helps me spend wisely—and saves my money, too.
F – Roshan
Developing wise saving habits is the key to financial security. Every week, I put a small part of
my allowance into a savings jar. At first, it didn’t seem like much, but after a few months, I had
enough for a new pair of shoes. I know that saving regularly—even a little—can help me prepare
for bigger goals. Having savings allows me to handle emergencies and plan for future expenses
like education or travel.
